;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]-linked militants attack a police station in [[South Kalimantan]], [[Indonesia]], killing an officer. One of the militants is shot dead as he tries to attack other policemen. [https://jakartaglobe.id/news/suspected-is-militants-attack-police-post-kill-officer-in-south-kalimantan (''Jakarta Globe'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Armenia]]
***[[Prime Minister of Armenia|Prime Minister]] [[Nikol Pashinyan]], his wife and their four children test positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-armenia-pm/armenian-pm-pashinyan-tests-positive-for-coronavirus-idUSKBN2381IC (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
***The annual [[Memorials for the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests#Hong Kong|Tiananmen Square massacre vigil]] in [[Hong Kong]] is banned for the first time since 1990 citing health concerns due to COVID-19. The [[Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China]], who organize the vigil, say the ban signals the end of Hong Kong's "[[one country, two systems]]". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-52877411 (BBC News)]
*[[Kivu Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] reports six new cases of [[ebola]], and [[UNICEF]] reports five deaths, in a renewed outbreak of the disease in [[Mbandaka]], [[Province of Équateur|Équateur Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/01/health/ebola-outbreak-congo-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;International relations
*[[United States–Zimbabwe relations]], [[George Floyd protests]]
**[[Zimbabwe]] summons the U.S. [[Envoy (title)#Popular parlance|envoy]] for comments by [[U.S. National Security Advisor]] [[Robert C. O'Brien]] suggesting that Zimbabwe is among "foreign adversaries" that could face retaliation for trying to foment unrest in the U.S. over the [[killing of George Floyd]]. [https://apnews.com/58e2082c8af14e376e89a366348ce262 (AP News)]

;Law and crime
*[[United States racial unrest (2020–2023)|United States racial unrest]]
**[[George Floyd protests]]
***[[Shooting of James Scurlock]]
****Prosecutors conclude a bar owner who fatally shot a protester during [[George Floyd protests|protests]] in [[Omaha, Nebraska]], acted in self-defense and therefore will not press charges against him. [https://www.omaha.com/news/crime/no-charges-will-be-filed-against-omaha-bar-owner-who-fatally-shot-protester-don-kleine/article_8e71702d-d5bf-544e-9fac-26108ac81a24.html (''Omaha World-Herald'')]
***[[Shooting of David McAtee]]
****Police and [[Kentucky National Guard|National Guard]] troops open fire on a group of protesters after allegedly being fired upon in [[Louisville, Kentucky]], resulting in the death of David McAtee, a local barbecue shop owner. An investigation is ongoing, while the LMPD Chief has been fired, as the officers involved in the shooting did not have their body cameras turned on. [https://apnews.com/3804be7642245883e6987f402e9e6302 (Associated Press)]
***[[George Floyd protests in Washington, D.C.]]
****An active duty [[military police]] [[battalion]] of 200 to 250 troops are deployed in the [[United States|U.S.]] capital [[Washington, D.C.]], to provide security as protests continue. Defense officials say the troops are from [[Fort Bragg]] in [[North Carolina]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/01/politics/troops-deploying-washington-dc/index.html?utm_source=feedburner&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=Feed%3A+rss%2Fcnn_allpolitics+%28RSS%3A+CNN+-+Politics%29 (CNN)]
***Forty cities across the United States impose overnight curfews in order to quell the violence from the protests. [https://www.cnn.com/us/live-news/george-floyd-protests-05-31-20/h_e876f5637c75c43d696fd72e881ed21d (CNN)]
***Two protesters are shot and killed during riots in [[Davenport, Iowa]]. In a separate incident, a police vehicle is [[ambush]]ed, resulting in the wounding of an officer. [https://eu.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/crime-and-courts/2020/06/01/davenport-iowa-rioting-two-people-shot-dead-police-officers-ambushed/5306484002/ (''The Des Moines Register'')]
***Two bystanders are shot and killed by "outside agitators" during protests in [[Cicero, Illinois]]. [https://chicago.cbslocal.com/2020/06/01/chaos-in-cicero-2-bystanders-shot-dead-in-one-incident-liquor-store-looting-suspects-caught-hiding-in-another/ (CBS Chicago)]
***Police shoot and kill an armed man wearing [[body armor]] at a protest in [[Las Vegas]]. In another incident, a policeman is shot and critically injured. [https://eu.rgj.com/story/news/2020/06/01/las-vegas-protest-george-floyd-black-lives-matter-protesters-trump-tower/5312668002/ (''Reno Gazette Journal'')]
***Anonymous sources suggest [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] is considering invoking the 1807 [[Insurrection Act]] to deploy the [[United States Armed Forces|military]] to respond to protests throughout the country. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/trump-considering-move-invoke-insurrection-act-n1221326 (NBC News)]
***Four [[Metropolitan Police Department, City of St. Louis|police]] officers are shot in [[St. Louis]] amid rioting in the downtown area of the city. [https://nypost.com/2020/06/02/four-police-officers-shot-in-st-louis-amid-chaos-and-looting/ (''New York Post'')]
**An independent [[autopsy]] concludes [[George Floyd]] [[Murder of George Floyd|died]] of "[[Asphyxia|asphyxiation]] from sustained pressure" and that there was "neck and back compression that led to a lack of blood flow to the brain" and that Floyd died at the scene of his arrest and not at the hospital, contradicting the [[Hennepin County, Minnesota]] [[coroner]]'s report. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/06/01/george-floyd-independent-autopsy-findings-released-monday/5307185002/ (''USA Today'')]
**Two police vehicles drive into a crowd of protesters in [[New York (state)|New York]]. Similar vehicle incidents also occur in [[Denver]] and [[Minneapolis]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/06/01/george-floyd-protests-cars-vehicles-plowing-into-demonstrations/5308969002/ (''USA Today'')]
